input: n,k,maxPts are integers with 0 <= k <= n <=10000 and 1 <= maxPts <=10000. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A Python float/JavaScript Number approximation to the probability that a process starting at 0, repeatedly drawing an independent uniform integer 1..maxPts while its score is below k, stops with score <=n. k=0 or n covering every possible terminal score returns 1. The final approximation is clamped into [0,1].
mutation_aliasing: Only scalar inputs are supplied. A private probability table and rolling active-state window are allocated; no randomness is sampled and no instance state persists.
numeric: Integer indices are exact. Probability division, summation and subtraction use ordinary binary64 floating arithmetic, so intermediate cancellation/rounding is possible. The official public tolerance is 1e-5, but no numerical-error bound or tolerance pass has been established by execution. Final clamping only enforces the probability range; it is NOT evidence of numerical correctness. Exact rational output is not claimed.
complexity: O(n+1) time and O(n+1) auxiliary table storage, or O(1) for an early certain-probability branch. Each state receives mass from the moving window of earlier scores still below k. Terminal scores contribute to answer, not future draw mass; outgoing active terms are removed once. No Monte Carlo sampling or O(n*maxPts) transition table is used.
